messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PAGING #eng-oncall — GPU pool us-west-2-gpu-pool1: node-drain-rate >= 2 in 10m; ECC errors rising (per-node avg 0.6 -> 2.1). Estimated capacity impact ~12%. PagerDuty incident PD-4241 created.

Ashwin P: acked. I’m on it — standing up quick triage. tagging @Maria H for ECC/thermal context.

Maria H: looking at telemetry now. ECC error spikes line up with a burst of node drains starting ~10m ago. VRAM usage looks normal on affected nodes, thermal_throttle spikes on two nodes.

Ashwin P: can you paste the nvml/errors? want to confirm uncorrectable vs corrected.

Maria H: paste from gpu-health logs: 
```
[2025-09-09T14:01:12Z] nvml: ECC_UNCORRECTABLE on gpu-uw2-gpu-03: count=1
[2025-09-09T14:03:05Z] nvml: ECC_CORRECTED on gpu-uw2-gpu-07: count=4
[2025-09-09T14:05:27Z] thermal: GPU 03 throttle_temp=95C state=throttling
[2025-09-09T14:07:31Z] node-drain: gw-drain initiated for gpu-uw2-gpu-03 (evac 6 pods)
```
Looks like 03 has the worst mix (uncorrectable + thermal).

Ashwin P: ok. immediate mitigation: 1) mark gpu-uw2-gpu-03 unschedulable and schedule reboot. 2) route critical traffic off pool to fallback pool (dedicated-fallback-usw2) — apply weight reduction 0.2 -> 0.0 for pool1 for 10m. 3) scale up spare pool by +2 nodes. Doing 1 and 2 now.

pagerduty-bot: Incident PD-4241 acknowledged by Ashwin P.

Kevin L: I can pick up alert tuning/actions after you finish the emergency steps. If this is hardware, we'll need RTX-squad looped.

Ashwin P: done with marking node unschedulable and triggering reboot job (job id: reboot-17675). Routing rule updated: `rb scale-weight us-west-2-gpu-pool1 --weight 0.0 --duration 10m`

Maria H: thermal spikes decreasing on node 03 after lower load, but ECC uncorrectable still present. We should treat uncorrectable ECC as hardware failure and follow chip-replacement runbook if it persists after reboot.

Ashwin P: agree. we should also reduce noise from flapping alerts. Current alert rules are tripping on single-sample ECC spikes; that's leading to noisy pages for transient corrected ECCs. Proposal: add dampening + composite conditions: require either (a) uncorrectable ECC >= 1 in 5m OR (b) corrected ECC >= 5 in 10m AND node-drain-rate >= 1 in 5m. Also add a 3-sample consecutive requirement for corrected ECC.

Kevin L: that sounds good. I’ll submit the change to alerting. Suggested Grafana alert snippet: 
```yaml
# grafana alert rule (draft)
- alert: GPU_ECC_Composite
  expr: |
    (increase(gpu_nvml_ecc_uncorrectable_total[5m]) >= 1) or 
    ((increase(gpu_nvml_ecc_corrected_total[10m]) >= 5) and (increase(node_drain_events[5m]) >= 1))
  for: 3m
  labels:
    severity: page
  annotations:
    summary: "GPU ECC composite alert (requires composite conditions)"
```
Add a dampening window of 3 eval cycles (for = 3m).

Maria H: also recommend separate non-paging warning for thermal_throttle > 0 for >5m, and a paging rule only if thermal_throttle > 0 AND drain-rate > 0. We want to avoid pages for brief thermal bump while investigating root-cause.

Ashwin P: +1. Can we also create a small dashboard panel for the raid: ECC rate, thermal_temp, drain_events, vram_alloc% in one row so oncall can eyeball quickly? Right now we open 3 panels across dashboards.

Kevin L: I’ll create a compact GPU health dashboard in the eng-oncall folder with these panels and add it to the incident runbook link. Will do before EOD UTC.

Maria H: runbook callouts to add: how to interpret uncorrectable vs corrected, nvml CLI commands to dump ECC counters, steps to mark unschedulable, hardware escalation steps and contact list for RTX-squad. Also include commands: 
```bash
# check ECC counters
kubectl exec -it gpu-uw2-gpu-03 -- nvml-summarize || nvml-summarize --json
# drain node
kubectl cordon gpu-uw2-gpu-03 && kubectl drain gpu-uw2-gpu-03 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data
```

Ashwin P: assigning action items: Kevin = implement alert rule + dashboard + PR to grafana repo. Maria = update runbook with snippets above and hardware escalation. I’ll follow up on reboots and postmortem.

Kevin L: I’ll open PR #3824 with the alert rule and dashboard JSON. ETA 4h.

Maria H: I’ll update runbook and add a checklist for post-reboot verification (nvml counters cleared, no further uncorrectable in 30m).

Ashwin P: handoff — I need to step off the next rotation in 10m. Kevin, you are primary oncall for the remainder of PD-4241. Please ping me if any new uncorrectable events after reboot.

Kevin L: taking over. ack. I’ll also schedule a 30m postmortem + tuning sync for tomorrow 1600 UTC.

Ashwin P: thanks team. marking incident as in mitigation. follow-ups: PR to alerting, dashboard, runbook, postmortem notes. :white_check_mark:

Maria H: note for postmortem: consider adding metric for transient-corrected-ecc-rate to be visible (we had corrected spikes that would be noisy under current rules).

Kevin L: noted. adding to postmortem agenda.

pagerduty-bot: Incident PD-4241 status updated: Mitigated -> Monitoring (assigned to Kevin L).

Maria H: last note — AWS host-level telemetry shows a recent firmware update pattern for the rack containing gpu-uw2-gpu-03 two days ago. Might be correlated; I’ll attach host firmware delta to postmortem.

Ashwin P: good catch. include in notes. all right handing off now.

Kevin L: thanks Ashwin — picking up. I’ll post the PR link and dashboard id when ready.

Maria H: thanks — I’ll follow up on runbook PR.

end of thread
